There are things that are not perfect about Voat's user interface, sure. But what's the rationale behind making a browser extension versus just adding those features to Voat directly? After all Voat is open source and seems very open to contributions.
Why make VES instead of adding the features to Voat directly?

Not the VES dev, and while I hope for more people to contribute code directly to Voat, there are some benefits to an independent browser extension:

  • faster iterations — you don’t have to wait for your code to be merged
  • easier to write high-level code — subjective, but many web devs may find it easier to write small chunks of UI code in JavaScript, than digging into Voat’s C#/ASP.NET. I personally am not familiar with C# and so I’ve only managed to contribute trivial fixes so far.

Of course there are also drawbacks, like extension data being local and inconvenient to transfer, and disparity between those who use the extension and those who do not (RES suffers from both of these effects).

I've been continuing my quest to conquer my PTW List. This week I knocked out a big one:

Steins;Gate (1-24/24) - MAL | Streaming

So this has been on my plan to watch list for a while. It was probably one of the first shows I added. So why I never got around to watching it I don't know. But there was a rewatch going on and I decided now is the ime to start watching. And holy hell have I been missing out.

I was not able to stop watching. After every episode ended I couldn't wait to watch the next. So keeping with the rewatch and watching only one episode per day didn't really work out :P

The story was absolutely amazing. It started out strong with likeable characters and a fun and interesting plot. Then at the point when it completely turned on it's head and became more of a thriller. This is probably the best anime, movie or tv-show that have dealt with time travel I've seen, except maybe Back to the Future.

The characters were as I said great and very likeable. They were very well written and you can connect with them right away. The sound was amazing as well. The voice acting was top notch, the OP was awesome and so was the ED. The art departmend is were it lacked the most but it is still very well done and fits the atmosphere perfectly.

This anime 100% deservs the praise it has gotten. I can't believe I've shoved it aside for so long. I went in with high expectations and it went waaaay beyond those. I can't wait to knock out more of the big ones.

Love Live! School Idol Project Second Season (1-13/13) MAL

I watched Love Live! back in winter when I was writing a review for The IdolM@ster so that I could have a better grasp of the whole Idol genre. It was certainly cute and enjoyable, but dismissable.

Took me a while to get to the Second Season, and I didn't plan on marathoning it. I planned to just poke away at a few episodes here and a few episodes there.

But no plan survives first contact.

Love Live! Second Season is a huge step above above the first season which was already fairly good. All the girls receive great developments, and I felt like every episode I had a new favorite girl.

The Second Season still relies on 3d animation for most of the dance scenes, but it looks smoother and just overall better than it did in the first season.

If you've enjoyed other Idol shows, or just want lots of cute girls doing cute things (and have already seen all of K-On!) this is a great show.
